section: Opposition precision and inferior king-and-pawn defense

positions.title: A c-pawn push changes the opposition — Pa2
positions.sourceLabel: P102 · Technical opposition and move order
positions.prompt: King opposition changes when the attacker goes via e4 or c4. The c3 pawn remains a reserve tempo but the defender can contest c4 and d5. White keeps a2 as an outside reserve tempo. Work both king routes and identify when an apparent pawn win gives the defender a tempo.
positions.replyReason: ...Kd6 and ...Kd5 actively oppose the escorting king; after c4 the newly advanced pawn may be attacked by the black king. In this variation, White keeps a2 as an outside reserve tempo.
positions.continuationReason: At the fifth ply White has increased pawn space, but Black is close enough to contest c4. The recorded five plies do not prove a forced promotion.
positions.explanation: A c-pawn push changes the opposition. Five-ply line d4e4 e6d6 e4f5 d6d5 c3c4. Resistance d4c4 e6d6 c4b5 d6d5 c3c4. Plausible different choice c3c4 e6d6 d4e4. King opposition changes when the attacker goes via e4 or c4. The c3 pawn remains a reserve tempo but the defender can contest c4 and d5. ...Kd6 and ...Kd5 actively oppose the escorting king; after c4 the newly advanced pawn may be attacked by the black king. Endpoint: White has increased pawn space, but Black is close enough to contest c4. The recorded five plies do not prove a forced promotion. Misconception: A fourth-rank passer is not automatically protected when the opposing king controls its new square. Pawn reserve: White keeps a2 as an outside reserve tempo. A concrete two-king draw after liquidation is exact only in the pure case; other WDL values require independent proof.

positions.title: The last dangerous pawn and the active king — one pawn each
positions.sourceLabel: P102 · Defending the worse pawn ending
positions.prompt: The defender's black a3 pawn can give a checking threat on a2, but White's king may capture the pawn if it chooses its square accurately. Only one pawn per side: an immediate complete liquidation would leave bare kings. Work both king routes and identify when an apparent pawn win gives the defender a tempo.
positions.replyReason: ...a2 attacks the white king on b1; Kxa2 captures it without entering the black king's attack from b4. In this variation, Only one pawn per side: an immediate complete liquidation would leave bare kings.
positions.continuationReason: At the fifth ply White retains its b-pawn after the capture. The king positions must still be evaluated for conversion or a draw.
positions.explanation: The last dangerous pawn and the active king. Five-ply line a1b1 a3a2 b1a2 b4c5 a2b3. Resistance a1b1 a3a2 b1a1 b4c5 a1a2. Plausible different choice a1b1 b4c5 b2b4. The defender's black a3 pawn can give a checking threat on a2, but White's king may capture the pawn if it chooses its square accurately. ...a2 attacks the white king on b1; Kxa2 captures it without entering the black king's attack from b4. Endpoint: White retains its b-pawn after the capture. The king positions must still be evaluated for conversion or a draw. Misconception: Immediately exchanging the last two pawns by bxa3 Kxa3 would be a draw in the pure case; avoid giving the opposing king a free recapture. Pawn reserve: Only one pawn per side: an immediate complete liquidation would leave bare kings. A concrete two-king draw after liquidation is exact only in the pure case; other WDL values require independent proof.
